Question: How can I get rid of overthinking?
Old_Answer: Overthinking arises only when you're not sure about your decision. Suppose you want to message your old school friend who wasn't polite to you the last time you spoke. Now you start to wonder if sending them a message is a good idea: Will they react badly? Will they be rude again, or will they be like the person who used to sit next to you in class? In this situation, there are only two options: There is no third option. If you're going to do something, be 100% sure about it, not 50% or 60%, but a full 100%. If you choose to do it, accept it entirely; if you choose not to, let it go completely and never dwell on it again. ~ Overthinking happens only when you start considering a third option between yes and no. On the other hand, love is a profound, enduring emotion built on a foundation of trust, affection, and deep understanding. Love requires time and effort to cultivate; it involves a mature bond where you accept someone wholly, flaws and all. Love goes beyond the surface and is characterized by genuine concern for the other person's well-being and happiness. Unlike attraction, love fosters a sense of security and loyalty, often leading to commitments that withstand the tests of time and adversity. While attraction can ignite the flame, love is the steady warmth that keeps it alive. In essence, think of attraction as the initial spark, often driven by physical traits and excitement, while love is the enduring fire that thrives on emotional intimacy and shared experiences. The two can exist independently—one can feel attraction without falling in love and vice versa. Understanding this distinction can help navigate personal relationships more mindfully, ensuring that we build connections that are not only passionate but also meaningful and lasting.

There was a teacher in our college who used to teach us corporate accounting. She was in her mid-20s and very arrogant. One day, the class was going fine, and she was teaching us. I noticed a pattern that she was only solving examples on black board and not any practical questions. At a particular example, the given solution in the book was incorrect. The teacher got confused and started writing every other figure to match the answer. Me: "Ma'am, why are you even looking at the solution given in the book?" Ma'am: "I think there is some error in the question. Just move to the next question. We will do it tomorrow.". (But at this point, her ego was hurt.) After some time, she suddenly said, "Why are you talking in the class?" Me: "I was just discussing the question." Ma'am: "I don't want to listen to anything. Come to the first row." Me: "Ma'am, I'm comfortable here." Ma'am: "I said come to the first row." Now I approached the first row. Me: "Ma'am, there are students sitting on both ends. How am I supposed to enter?" Ma'am: "Just jump over the bench." Me: "Ma'am, I'm not an athlete.". (Whole class starts laughing, but her ego is hurt again.) Now settled, seated in a chilling posture, the class is about to end. Ma'am: "You know, I have never met any student like you in my teaching career of 3 years." Me: "Ma'am, but what have I done?" Ma'am: "See, that's the problem. You are not even recognizing your mistake". Frontbechers sitting next to me: "Siddharth, say sorry to ma'am." Me: "But why? What is my mistake?" Ma'am: "You know, students like you don't deserve to be in this college." Me: "I don't want your suggestion." Ma'am: "You don't know how to behave in class and talk to teachers." Me: "I haven't asked for your opinion." Ma'am: "I don't want students like you. Don't ever again come to my class." Me: "Okay, I have no problem." After the class ends, everybody leaves the classrooms. I approached to her. (she in a hope I will apologize to her) Me: "Ma'am, as you said, don't come to my class. What about the 75% attendance requirement?" Ma'am: "I don't have any knowledge about it." Me: "Then what should I do? Can you give it to me in written?" Ma'am: "See, I never said you cannot come to my class. But please behave yourself" Me: "Okay, thank you, ma'am." (I thought the matter was resolved.) In the end of the semester, she gave only 10 marks out of 25 in internals 🥲. Her revenge was complete. ~ Siddharth Xyz
